# rtauargus.native

An R interface for [Tau-Argus](https://github.com/sdcTools/tauargus),
statistical disclosure control for tables and microdata.

This is a fork of INSEE's
[rtauargus](https://github.com/inseefrlab/rtauargus). Upstream launches
the legacy TauArgus.exe executable. This fork executes the same `.arb`
batches in process, through the native HiGHS-backed
[tauargus-engine](https://github.com/trygu/tauargus-engine). Function
names, arguments and return values follow upstream; see
[the compatibility guide](https://github.com/trygu/rtauargus.native/blob/master/docs/compatibility.md)
for the intentional
differences. The package is self-contained: the native engine and HiGHS
are bundled in it and build at install time, so there is one package to
install and no separate Tau-Argus installation required. After installing
the package, load `library(rtauargus.native)` and run the R functions.
There is no Tau-Argus executable path or external solver to configure.

## Documentation for this version

This README covers installation, native execution, a complete table
example and direct `.arb` batches for `rtauargus.native`. The
[compatibility guide](https://github.com/trygu/rtauargus.native/blob/master/docs/compatibility.md)
records the differences
from INSEE's package and the legacy Tau-Argus engine, including output
formats that are not implemented and possible differences in secondary
suppression patterns.

The high-level R interface builds on INSEE's rtauargus. Use its
[full function reference](https://inseefrlab.github.io/rtauargus/reference/index.html)
and [guides](https://inseefrlab.github.io/rtauargus/) for table and
microdata preparation, hierarchies, safety rules and linked tables.
The original authors' documentation remains the reference for those
inherited functions; this README explains how to use them with the
bundled native engine. Installed help is also available, for example
with `?tab_rtauargus` and `?run_arb`.

When following an upstream example:

- Load `rtauargus.native` instead of `rtauargus`.
- Skip the separate Tau-Argus installation and
  `options(rtauargus.tauargus_exe = ...)` configuration.
- Use the solver included in this package. No CPLEX or XPRESS
  installation or license is needed.
- Check the compatibility guide for execution and output differences.

The `tauargus_exe`, `logbook`, `verbose` and `...` arguments of
`run_arb()` remain accepted for backward compatibility and are ignored.
Data paths, safety rules and other task-specific inputs still need to
be supplied as in the original R interface.

## Installation

Install the package from CRAN:

```r
install.packages("rtauargus.native")
```

The package is self-contained: the native engine and HiGHS are bundled
in it and built at install time. CRAN distributes a source tarball; on
Windows a prebuilt binary is available from CRAN's binary repository,
while on macOS and Linux the package installs from source and compiles
the bundled engine at install time, which needs CMake >= 3.16 and a
C++17 compiler (on macOS, the Xcode command line tools). Its R
dependencies install from CRAN as usual.

To install the latest version from [GitHub
Releases](https://github.com/trygu/rtauargus.native/releases) instead,
each release (tags `r-v*`) contains one binary per platform, a source
tarball and a `release-manifest.json` with the SHA-256 hash of every
asset. The binaries are built for R 4.5.3 (the `r4.5.3` in the file
name) and install without a compiler. The source tarball works with
other R versions and needs CMake >= 3.16 and a C++17 compiler.
Install the CRAN dependencies once first (on Linux they compile from
source, and `igraph` takes a few minutes):

```r
install.packages(c("purrr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "data.table", "gdata",
                   "stringr", "rlang", "zoo", "sdcHierarchies",
                   "igraph", "lifecycle"))
```

The URLs below select release `r-v0.6.3`, whose R package carries
version `1.3.6-0.6.3`. For another release, take the asset names from
its release page. The release tag and the R package version are separate
identifiers.

Windows:

```r
install.packages(
  "https://github.com/trygu/rtauargus.native/releases/download/r-v0.6.3/rtauargus.native_1.3.6-0.6.3.zip",
  repos = NULL, type = "binary")
library(rtauargus.native)
```

The Windows binary follows the CRAN file name form
`rtauargus.native_<version>.zip`: R's zip installer derives the
package directory from the file name, so a platform-suffixed name
would install the package under the wrong directory.

macOS (Apple silicon; the release targets arm64):

```r
install.packages(
  "https://github.com/trygu/rtauargus.native/releases/download/r-v0.6.3/rtauargus.native_1.3.6-0.6.3_r4.5.3_macos-arm64.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL, type = "binary")
library(rtauargus.native)
```

Linux:

```r
install.packages(
  "https://github.com/trygu/rtauargus.native/releases/download/r-v0.6.3/rtauargus.native_1.3.6-0.6.3_r4.5.3_linux-x86_64.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL)
library(rtauargus.native)
```

`type = "binary"` is only supported on Windows and macOS. On Linux
the prebuilt tarball installs as a source package, so the argument
is omitted.

Source installation for supported R versions (builds the bundled
engine at install time):

```r
install.packages(
  "https://github.com/trygu/rtauargus.native/releases/download/r-v0.6.3/rtauargus.native_1.3.6-0.6.3.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL)
library(rtauargus.native)
```

## Package versions and upstream provenance

The development package records the imported INSEE revision in
`upstream.json`. Its package version combines the version from that
revision's `DESCRIPTION` with the native engine version, separated by a
hyphen. The INSEE component is currently `1.3.6`. It changes only after
new upstream code has been imported and reviewed.

Release `r-v0.6.0` predates this scheme and contains R packages numbered
`1.3.7`. R considers a composite starting with `1.3.6` older than `1.3.7`.
If you installed one of those files, explicitly install the new release
from its source or binary file; automatic version-based updates will not
select it. You can inspect your installed package with
`packageVersion("rtauargus.native")`.

## License

The assembled native package uses EUPL-1.2. INSEE's R frontend and HiGHS
retain their original MIT terms. Current source builds install a
`COPYRIGHTS` overview and the original component notices under `LICENSES`.

## Quick start

Once installed, the same R code runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. The
example below protects a small table with two primary safety rules
(minimum frequency and 1-85 dominance) and the default secondary
(modular) suppression:

```r
library(rtauargus.native)

act_size <- data.frame(
  ACTIVITY = c("01","01","01","02","02","02","06","06","06","Total","Total","Total"),
  SIZE = c("tr1","tr2","Total","tr1","tr2","Total","tr1","tr2","Total","tr1","tr2","Total"),
  VAL = c(100,50,150,30,20,50,60,40,100,190,110,300),
  N_OBS = c(10,5,15,2,5,7,8,6,14,20,16,36),
  MAX = c(20,15,20,20,10,20,16,38,38,20,38,38)
)

ex1 <- tab_rtauargus(
  act_size,
  dir_name = file.path(tempdir(), "tauargus_ex1"),
  files_name = "ex1",
  explanatory_vars = c("ACTIVITY", "SIZE"),
  safety_rules = "FREQ(3,10)|NK(1,85)",
  value = "VAL",
  freq = "N_OBS",
  maxscore = "MAX",
  totcode = c(ACTIVITY = "Total", SIZE = "Total"),
  verbose = FALSE
)
ex1
```

`tab_rtauargus()` writes the table input set (`.tab` values, `.rda`
metadata, `.arb` batch) into `dir_name`, runs the batch, writes the
published CSV and returns the input table with a `Status` column:

- `A`: primary secret, frequency rule
- `B`: primary secret, dominance rule (first contributor)
- `C`: primary secret, frequency rule with more than one contributor
- `D`: secondary secret
- `V`: valid, no masking needed

## Running your own .arb batch

The quick start call already wrote the table input set (`ex1.tab` for
the values, `ex1.rda` for the metadata) into `dir_name`. You can drive
that same input set from a hand-written batch with `run_arb()`; the
legacy batch grammar is a drop-in. This batch applies the same primary
and secondary rules and exports a pivot CSV with a status column
(`AS+`):

```r
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "tauargus_ex1")
arb <- file.path(dir, "ex1_hand.arb")
writeLines(c(
  sprintf('<OPENTABLEDATA> "%s"', file.path(dir, "ex1.tab")),
  sprintf('<OPENMETADATA> "%s"', file.path(dir, "ex1.rda")),
  '<SPECIFYTABLE> "ACTIVITY""SIZE"|"VAL"||',
  "<SAFETYRULE> FREQ(3,10)|NK(1,85)",
  "<READTABLE> 1",
  "<SUPPRESS> MOD(1,5,1,0,0)",
  sprintf('<WRITETABLE> (1,2,AS+,"%s")', file.path(dir, "ex1_hand.csv"))
), arb)

run_arb(arb)
read.csv(file.path(dir, "ex1_hand.csv"))
```

The lines follow the legacy grammar: `OPENTABLEDATA` / `OPENMETADATA`
open the input set, `SPECIFYTABLE` declares the explanatory and
response variables, `SAFETYRULE` sets the primary rules, `READTABLE`
loads the table and `SUPPRESS` runs the secondary suppression. The
four `WRITETABLE` fields are the table number, the output format
(1 plain CSV, 2 pivot CSV, 3 code value, 4 SBS, 5 intermediate),
option letters (`AS+` adds the Status column) and the output file.

`run_arb()` runs silently and returns `NULL` by default; the results
land in the output file. Pass `import = TRUE` to get a list of
data frames back into R.

To protect microdata instead of a pre-aggregated table, use
`micro_rtauargus()` (see the vignette `rtauargus_micro`).

## Checking the installed engine

```r
tauargus_engine_meta()        # engine commit + HiGHS version of this build
tauargus_version(new_tauargus())
```

Report the `tauargus_engine_meta()` output when filing a problem. The
native audit (CSP intervalle check) is exposed as `audit_jj(jjfile)`;
the front-end uses it through the engine object's `audit(tab)` method
and the `with_audit` table export.

## Ownership and development

- This repo owns the R front-end: package, tests, releases.
- The native engine and the R binding live in
  [tauargus-engine](https://github.com/trygu/tauargus-engine) and are
  pinned here as a git submodule (`tauargus-engine/`; the gitlink is
  the pin). Bump the submodule to the engine commit you want, then
  push.
- The release pipeline (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) stages the
  native layer into this package from the pinned source. Every run
  builds the package on Linux, macOS and Windows, then installs each
  built artifact in a fresh environment without a product checkout,
  runs the full test suite and the shared ex1 `.arb` job against it,
  and checks the installed engine metadata. On `r-v*` tags it
  additionally writes per-artifact SHA-256 manifests, verifies them
  (hashes, platform coverage, lockstep with the pinned engine) and
  publishes only the verified assets to the GitHub Release.
